title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Holiday: Thanksgiving
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect from 2 past Thanksgivings: x0.95 vs baseline; 2025: x0.91, 2024: x0.71, 2023: x0.81

drivers.name: Store closed Monday
drivers.evidence: Store closure on Monday reduces 1/7 of weekly sales; no direct past evidence, so shrunk to 5% impact

adjustment.analysis: Thanksgiving reduces demand (noise-adjusted x0.95), and the store closure on Monday further suppresses sales. The price increase (1.5%) is minor and unlikely to offset the holiday effect. The classical model's 0.95 multiplier is reasonable but doesn't account for the closure. Past data shows Thanksgiving weeks average x0.81 vs baseline, but the noise-adjusted estimate (x0.95) is more reliable. The closure likely reduces sales by ~5% (10% on Mon, but 1/7 of week). No promotion or other driver. Combine multiplicative: 0.95 × 0.95 = 0.90. Adjust toward 1.0 due to low evidence for closure impact. Final median adjusted to 0.92. Spreads unchanged: baseline uncertainty is well-calibrated.

It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
